questions.stem: What type of diagnostic recording is displayed in this grayscale tracing?

explanation.summary: The panelled layout of limb and precordial leads printed on standard ECG graph paper identifies this as a 12-lead electrocardiogram used to evaluate rhythm and conduction abnormalities such as heart blocks.
explanation.whyCorrect: The panelled layout of limb and precordial leads printed on standard ECG graph paper identifies this as a 12-lead electrocardiogram used to evaluate rhythm and conduction abnormalities such as heart blocks.

questions.stem: These leads show a broad 'W' morphology in V1 and an 'M' morphology in V6 with a widened QRS. What conduction abnormality does this pattern indicate?

explanation.summary: The 'WiLLiaM' mnemonic applies: a W in V1 and an M in V6 with a QRS > 120 ms indicates left bundle branch block, in which delayed left ventricular activation reshapes the complexes in these leads.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 'WiLLiaM' mnemonic applies: a W in V1 and an M in V6 with a QRS > 120 ms indicates left bundle branch block, in which delayed left ventricular activation reshapes the complexes in these leads.

questions.topicName: Heart Blocks: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis and Treatment
questions.stem: V1 shows an rSR' complex and V6 shows a qRs with a widened QRS. Which conduction defect produces this appearance?

explanation.summary: The 'MaRRoW' mnemonic applies: an M-shaped rSR' in V1 and a W-like qRs in V6 with QRS > 120 ms indicate right bundle branch block, reflecting delayed right ventricular activation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 'MaRRoW' mnemonic applies: an M-shaped rSR' in V1 and a W-like qRs in V6 with QRS > 120 ms indicate right bundle branch block, reflecting delayed right ventricular activation.

questions.stem: In the conduction pathway shown, which structure normally imposes a deliberate delay before the impulse reaches the ventricles?

explanation.summary: The AV node slows conduction between atria and ventricles, allowing time for atrial contraction to complete ventricular filling before ventricular depolarization. Excessive slowing or block at this node produces AV heart block.
explanation.whyCorrect: The AV node slows conduction between atria and ventricles, allowing time for atrial contraction to complete ventricular filling before ventricular depolarization. Excessive slowing or block at this node produces AV heart block.

questions.stem: This 12-lead ECG shows a rapid, regular, wide-complex tachycardia. What is the most likely rhythm?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

explanation.summary: A regular wide-complex (broad QRS) tachycardia at a fast rate is ventricular tachycardia until proven otherwise, arising from an ectopic ventricular focus below the AV node.
explanation.whyCorrect: A regular wide-complex (broad QRS) tachycardia at a fast rate is ventricular tachycardia until proven otherwise, arising from an ectopic ventricular focus below the AV node.

questions.stem: This chest radiograph shows a radio-opaque device implanted in the left pectoral region with leads extending toward the cardiac silhouette. What is this device?

explanation.summary: A pulse generator in a left infraclavicular pocket with radio-opaque leads coursing into the right heart chambers is the classic appearance of an implanted cardiac pacemaker (or ICD) on chest X-ray.
explanation.whyCorrect: A pulse generator in a left infraclavicular pocket with radio-opaque leads coursing into the right heart chambers is the classic appearance of an implanted cardiac pacemaker (or ICD) on chest X-ray.

questions.stem: This 12-lead ECG shows a wide-complex tachycardia in which the QRS complexes vary in amplitude and appear to twist around the baseline. What is this rhythm?

explanation.summary: A polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with QRS complexes that appear to twist around the isoelectric baseline is torsades de pointes, classically associated with QT prolongation.
explanation.whyCorrect: A polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with QRS complexes that appear to twist around the isoelectric baseline is torsades de pointes, classically associated with QT prolongation.

questions.stem: This 12-lead ECG demonstrates an irregular wide-complex tachycardia with continuously changing QRS morphology and no consistent baseline. What does this tracing represent?

explanation.summary: Beat-to-beat variation in QRS shape and amplitude in a fast wide-complex rhythm indicates polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, an unstable arrhythmia that can degenerate into ventricular fibrillation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beat-to-beat variation in QRS shape and amplitude in a fast wide-complex rhythm indicates polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, an unstable arrhythmia that can degenerate into ventricular fibrillation.

questions.stem: This defibrillator rhythm strip shows chaotic, irregular, disorganized deflections with no identifiable QRS complexes or organized rhythm. What is this?

explanation.summary: Chaotic, irregular waveforms without discrete QRS complexes represent ventricular fibrillation, a disorganized quivering of the ventricles that produces no cardiac output and requires immediate defibrillation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chaotic, irregular waveforms without discrete QRS complexes represent ventricular fibrillation, a disorganized quivering of the ventricles that produces no cardiac output and requires immediate defibrillation.

questions.stem: This diagram shows an implanted device with a pulse generator connected to leads terminating in the right atrium and right ventricle. What is the primary function of this device?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To mechanically pump blood in place of the ventricle

choices.label: C
choices.text: To electrically pace the myocardium and maintain heart rate

choices.label: D
choices.text: To filter emboli from the venous return

explanation.summary: The device is a cardiac pacemaker: a pulse generator delivers electrical impulses through transvenous leads to the atrium and ventricle, triggering myocardial depolarization to maintain an adequate heart rate.
explanation.whyCorrect: The device is a cardiac pacemaker: a pulse generator delivers electrical impulses through transvenous leads to the atrium and ventricle, triggering myocardial depolarization to maintain an adequate heart rate.
